Cc: David Kim <david@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Custody routing and subprocessor enrollment — next steps

Hi Samir / MediVerse legal team,

Thanks again for the discussion this morning. Per our call, this thread captures the concrete operational plan Redwood will follow to satisfy your no-training and custody requirements, plus the timing for enrolling the new EU subprocessor you asked about. We want to make sure the plan is explicit so your legal/ops teams can sign off.

Summary (high level):
- Capture classification: we will tag interactions at ingress (structured payload vs free-text) and route PII/PHI-marked objects to tenant-scoped ephemeral KV (no persistence beyond TTL) unless you opt into SFTP export.
- No-training toggle semantics: when the MV no-train flag is on, payloads will be excluded from all model fine-tuning pipelines and from long-term telemetry used for model improvement. Short-lived telemetry for infra health (latency/trace) is retained for 7 days, aggregated and redacted.
- Subprocessor enrollment: the new EU analytics partner (requested by MediVerse) will be added to our Subprocessor Registry after attestation and a 10-business-day review window. Enrollment is gated on the signed attestation (attached).

Requested next steps from MediVerse:
1) Confirm the capture classification mapping (attached worksheet). If anything should be routed to SFTP by default, mark the column.
2) Legal: sign the subprocessor attestation addendum (we can DocuSign).
3) Ops: confirm the on-prem SFTP endpoint and SSH fingerprint for exports (if you want the SFTP path enabled).

Attachments: ops-custody-checklist.xlsx (routing matrix), subprocessor-attestation-template.pdf (redlined addendum for subprocessor enrollment).

If you approve, Kimberly will schedule a 30-min ops handoff and David will own the rollout checklist on our side.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

--

Rachel — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we sign anything: 

1) The no-training toggle: please confirm that it applies at the tenant level (i.e., an account-level flag that prevents our interactions from entering any model improvement artifact stores). We need a written assurance this is enforced by policy and not just process.

2) Telemetry retention: 7 days for infra sounds fine, but can we get a short description of what is considered "aggregated and redacted" telemetry? We are particularly concerned about any free-text snippets ending up in logs.

3) Subprocessor timeline: 10 business days looks fine. Legal wants to confirm the attestation includes a clause prohibiting derivative model training and requiring EU data residency for the subprocessor.

4) Export path: we'll provide SFTP details; that will be our preferred path for periodic exports.

I can have our legal counsel provide a brief redline if needed. Please confirm whether you will accept a MediVerse redline to the attestation or if you prefer to push a revised Redwood version.

Samir
CTO, MediVerse Health
cto@mediverse.com

Samir — great questions. Quick answers inline, and I also included next steps for ops acceptance.

1) Tenant-level enforcement: confirmed. The no-train flag is enforced at the request router and enforced by the serving runtime policy layer. When set, requests from that tenant are annotated and excluded from any downstream training/export pipelines. We will provide a short technical note describing where the flag is applied in the request path (attached to the Drive link).

2) Aggregated/redacted telemetry: short description below —
- What we collect for infra health: request latency histogram, per-route error counters, anonymized model load metrics.
- What we redact: we never persist free-text user inputs in logs when no-train is set. Short-lived traces may contain truncated identifiers (sha256 prefixes) to correlate requests; full payloads are dropped.

3) Attestation content: we can accept MediVerse redlines, but to speed review we suggest you use our attestation template (attached) and highlight changes. The running requirement from Redwood: any subprocessor handling MediVerse data under the attestation must sign an operational pledge that disallows derivative training on cleared data and commits EU data residency for the covered assets.

4) Export path: Kimberly — can you confirm ops availability for a 30-min handoff tomorrow 12/23? We will need the SFTP endpoint + fingerprint, and a contact for escalation.

Next steps (Redwood owners):
- Rachel: provide 1-page technical note showing enforcement point and log-redaction behavior (will post to Drive by EOD).
- David: complete the ops-custody-checklist with routing defaults and TTLs (draft attached).
- Kimberly: schedule handoff and collect SFTP details from MediVerse.

If that works, we can prepare a DocuSign addendum for signature.

Thanks,
Rachel

Hi Samir / MediVerse ops/legal — I'm Kimberly on Redwood's customer ops team. Thanks for the prompt reply — I can do the handoff tomorrow at 10:30 AM PT (12/23 10:30 PT). Please send the SFTP hostname, port (if non-standard), and the SSH host key fingerprint into this thread before the call.

A few practical notes for your engineers:
- Default routing: unless you mark otherwise in the routing matrix, free-text chat inputs will be sent to the tenant-scoped ephemeral KV with TTL=24 hours. SFTP exports are run nightly if enabled.
- SFTP verification: we will verify the host key before enabling automated exports and we will do a test transfer with a small, non-PII file.
- Attestation: legal — once we receive your redline or signed attestation we will begin the 10-business-day subprocessor review. If you choose to add the EU partner as a subprocessor during review, data will remain onshore (EU) by default; only the SFTP export path will move data off-platform under your control.

Action items for MediVerse before the handoff call:
1) Send SFTP details + fingerprint.
2) Indicate any fields in the routing matrix that should be defaulted to SFTP.
3) Legal: attach any redlines to the attestation PDF or indicate you accept our template.

I'll post the meeting invite to calendar and include a short ops checklist for the call. Looking forward to wrapping this up.
